title: heuristics-latency-sleuth-notes
content:
Purpose
-----
Personal debugging scratchpad for the embeddings+rerank flakiness we saw starting Feb 16. Primary symptoms: intermittent dimension mismatch errors from client SDK and periodic latency spikes on /v1/rerank when candidate count > ~400. This is a fast log of commands tried, traces observed, ad-hoc experiments, and prioritised next steps. Treat as ephemeral notes; I'll move useful items to INF-5234 later.

Breadcrumb timeline (high level)
-----------------------------
- 2026-02-16 09:40 PST: First customer report (internal) — rerank call returning 500 error; error message: "embedding dimensionality mismatch".
- 2026-02-17: Multiple similar tickets; pattern: only affects some calls from region eu-west1 and some requests from SDK v1.4.2.
- 2026-02-18: I reproduced locally with a synthetic batch of 512 candidates. Observed latency spikes ~1.1s up from baseline ~60ms.
- 2026-02-20: Deployed a logging patch to log embedding vector length at network boundary. Confirmed sporadic 128-d vectors returned from upstream model while expected 1536-d.

Reproducer commands (local)
--------------------------
1) Minimal curl to rerank endpoint (simulate candidate=512):
   curl -X POST \n     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n     -d '{"query": "How to set up SSO?", "candidates": ["cand1","cand2", ... repeated 512 ...] }' \n     https://api.redwood.test/v1/rerank

2) Python quick shape-check (useful to detect client-side truncation):
   from requests import post
   import json

   r = post(url, headers=headers, json=payload).json()
   emb = r.get('query_embedding')
   print('query emb len', len(emb))
   for i,c in enumerate(r.get('candidate_embeddings', [])):
       if len(c) != 1536:
           print('bad candidate', i, 'len', len(c))

Observed output snippets (logs)
------------------------------
- HTTP 200 but payload included: "candidate_embeddings": [[...], [...], ..., [0.123, 0.02]] (last vector length=128)
- Server-side warning (in logs): "model X returned vector length 128 for inference id=abc123"
- SRE trace of tail latency: percentiles for /v1/rerank on 2026-02-18
    p50 = 62ms, p90 = 110ms, p99 = 560ms, p999 = 1.12s
- Correlation: 90% of p999 spikes align with requests that included > 400 candidates; many of those go to model variant: text-embed-small-quantized-v2 (recently added to catalog).

Hypotheses (ranked)
-------------------
1) Model variant mismatch / graceful fallback bug: router sometimes falls back to a compact/quantized embedding model (128 dim) instead of the expected 1536-d model, but downstream code assumes fixed 1536 and doesn't handle differing dims, causing soft errors or extra processing that lengthens latency.
2) SDK client truncation: older SDK (v1.4.2) has a serialization bug that drops rows or compresses floats when payloads are large, only visible for big candidate arrays.
3) Memory pressure on serving node leads to loading a small model variant to satisfy capacity and increases CPU-based post-processing causing latency spikes.
4) Network-level partial response earlier in pipeline (proxy) that streams first N embeddings and then returns a compact fallback; curious but less likely.

Experiments / quick checks done
------------------------------
- Forced request routing to specific model by adding "model: text-embed-large-v1" header — reproduced with stable 1536 vectors and no dimension errors. Latency stayed normal. Suggests router variant selection matters.
- Replayed the same heavy-candidate request while pinning to quantized-small — got consistent 128-d vectors but latency was lower (since those models are tiny). So dimension difference isn't intrinsically causing latency spike; the spike occurs when router mixes variants or when a fallback happens mid-request.
- Sent identical requests from SDK v1.4.2 and local raw curl; reproduced only with SDK in ~30% of attempts. Collected SDK raw bytes (base64) and inspected: no truncation of array sections. SDK bug less likely but cannot be ruled out.
- Added additional server instrumentation (logging model_id used per inference, vector lengths, queue depth) on a canary host. Observed several requests labeled with two different model_ids in the same request lifecycle (e.g., initial embedding from model A then candidates scored by model B). That's suspicious (race or orchestration issue).

Quick root-cause theory (working)
--------------------------------
Router concurrency/race when handling large candidate sets: orchestration attempts to parallelize candidate embedding retrieval across multiple workers and, under specific timing, one worker returns embeddings from a different model variant (128-d) because its model cache was different. Downstream code assumes homogeneous dims and either throws or performs an expensive reshape/convert that causes p99/p999 latency. The mix of variants could also force an expensive cross-model re-embedding path.

Immediate mitigations attempted
-------------------------------
- Hotfix: enforce model homogeneity at router: if any worker responds with different dimension, mark request as failed fast with a clear error (instead of trying to massage). Deployed to canary group on 2026-02-24. Reduced noisy errors but did not eliminate spikes.
- Rate-limited heavy candidate requests at API gateway (temporary): denies > 1024 candidates, and adds header warning. Reduced load on tail nodes.

Longer-term fixes under consideration
------------------------------------
- Ensure model routing uses consistent pinned model per request (single decision made at entrypoint, used for all shards). Remove opportunistic per-shard fallbacks.
- Add strict schema validation of embedding lengths at network boundary and early fail with meaningful error to callers.
- Compatibility shim: if mixing dims is unavoidable, create deterministic up-/down-projection operators and measure their cost; evaluate viability.
- Add a unit/regression test in serving-runtime that simulates multi-shard returns with mixed models.

Next steps (priority ordered)
---------------------------
1) (Today) Add extra logs to canary: [request_id, chosen_model_at_entry, list(models_seen), candidate_count, worker_ids].
2) Write a small fuzz test that sends n=1000 randomized candidate counts across model variants to reproduce race locally. Attach to CI as flaky test to catch regressions. (Evan/Ravi)
3) Coordinate with infra to examine node-level model cache sync: are cached model lists inconsistent across shard pool? (Maya)
4) Proof-of-concept: route all shards for a request via single-model promise in the router; measure p99 impact on A/B canary.
5) Communicate temporary guidance to SDK teams: recommend pinning model in client request until fix shipped.

Notes to self / loose thoughts
-----------------------------
- The fact that quantized-small returns 128-d is expected; we need to be explicit in catalog that dims differ and ensure catalog metadata is enforced at routing time.
- Could be a recent change in model catalog rollout (Feb 10) that added the small quantized variant into some node pools; maybe pool labels not propagated.
- Ticket INF-5234 should capture customer-facing mitigation text and recommended code sample for SDKs.

Files I dumped / useful snippets location
--------------------------------------
- /tmp/repro_2026-02-18/requests.log (sample requests and full JSON payloads)
- /tmp/repro_2026-02-18/model-mapping.csv (observed model_id -> node mappings)
- PR with logging change: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/721 (linked above)

If anything else I should add here: quick copy/paste of customer error text, any relevant SLA impacts (we were under 99.9 overall but individual customers saw 5-10 minute slow windows).

-- Evan
